welcome.title: Welcome to protunel
welcome.body: This tour walks through tunnels, the Router, the terminal and settings. Press ← or → to move, Esc to close; replay it any time with F1 or from Settings › About.

mode.title: Choose your mode
mode.body: Switch modes in Settings › General. Simple mode gives you one Internal network switch, while Full mode gives you the tunnel, router, and terminal controls.

appearance.title: Preview a theme
appearance.body: Hover over a theme to preview it and click to keep it. Choose Follow system to set separate light and dark themes.

language.title: Change the language
language.body: Open the globe menu and choose English or Tiếng Việt.

linux-setup.title: Finish Linux setup
linux-setup.body: If this notice appears, follow the commands it shows to set up the credential vault or SSH agent.

tray.title: Keep tunnels running in the tray
tray.body: Close the main window to hide it while tunnels keep running. Reopen it from the tray, or choose Exit in the tray menu to quit.

add.title: Add an SSH tunnel
add.body: Choose Add tunnel and enter the server address, SSH port, and username. Review the server’s key fingerprint when you first connect.

add-auth.title: Choose how to sign in
add-auth.body: Choose a password, a private key file, or an SSH agent. Saved passwords and key passphrases go into your system credential vault.

add-socks.title: Set up a local proxy
add-socks.body: Enable SOCKS5 and point an application at the local port shown here. For a host you only use for SSH shells, leave SOCKS5 off.

add-jump.title: Connect through a jump host
add-jump.body: Choose a saved tunnel under Connect via to reach a private host through it. Connecting the destination brings up the jump chain for you.

list.title: Manage tunnels and forwards
list.body: Use a tunnel’s switch to connect it, or expand Forwards on its row to add a port forward while it’s running. Jump hosts group their dependent tunnels underneath them.

bulk.title: Search and connect in bulk
bulk.body: Press Ctrl+F to filter by name or host. The connect and disconnect buttons act on the entire list, including tunnels hidden by your search.

router.title: Route through one local proxy
router.body: Open Router to send traffic through one local SOCKS5 address. Rules choose a route for each connection.

router-enable.title: Start the router and copy its address
router-enable.body: Flip the switch on the status card, then copy the local SOCKS5 address for your application. The router connects a tunnel on demand when a rule sends traffic through it.

router-rules.title: Set rule priority
router-rules.body: Add a hostname wildcard, regex, or IP range and choose a tunnel, Direct, or Block. Move higher-priority rule cards up because the first enabled match wins.

router-log.title: Trace a routing decision
router-log.body: Open Log and find the destination to see the matched rule and where the connection went.

router-settings.title: Set the default route
router-settings.body: Open the router’s Settings tab to change its port and choose what happens when no rule matches.

router-proxy.title: Use the Windows system proxy
router-proxy.body: Enable the system proxy to send compatible apps through the router via PAC. Add addresses to the bypass list if those apps should connect to them directly.

router-pac.title: Copy the browser PAC URL
router-pac.body: Expand the Linux proxy instructions and copy the PAC URL into your browser’s automatic proxy settings. The instructions also show how to set up SOCKS5 for individual apps.

capture-launch.title: Launch an app through the router
capture-launch.body: Open Capture, select an executable, and add arguments if needed. Launch it from this form to send its traffic through the router.

capture-monitor.title: Check apps and their traffic
capture-monitor.body: Use the active list to find or stop a process. Check the log below it to see where the router sent each connection.

terminal.title: Open the SSH terminal
terminal.body: Click Terminal to open a separate window with your saved hosts. Use its own ? button for the walkthrough on tabs, splits, and broadcast.

settings.title: Find settings by subject
settings.body: Open Settings and use the side list to switch between General, Tunnels, Terminal, Backup, and About.

settings-reconnect.title: Adjust reconnection
settings-reconnect.body: Open Tunnels to set keepalives and reconnect behavior. Local ports stay reserved while a tunnel retries.

settings-terminal.title: Tune the terminal
settings-terminal.body: Open Terminal settings to adjust rendering and mouse behavior, or set up command suggestions and long-command notifications here.

settings-config.title: Export or import a configuration
settings-config.body: Use Export to create a configuration file and set a passphrase to include encrypted credentials. Use Import to review what will be applied before confirming.

settings-hosts.title: Review trusted hosts
settings-hosts.body: Open the trusted hosts list on Backup to inspect saved SSH fingerprints. Forget a key here when you’re ready to verify its replacement on the next connection.

settings-about.title: Find your version and updates
settings-about.body: Open About to check your installed version and see how updates are delivered for your installation.

term-hosts.title: Open a host
term-hosts.body: Choose a saved host in the sidebar to open its shell, or use + beside Hosts to add one. Expand a jump host to see the hosts that connect through it, or show the sidebar with Ctrl+Shift+S.

term-select.title: Open several hosts together
term-select.body: Turn on Select hosts beside the Hosts heading, choose your hosts, then open them in one tiled tab.

term-tabs.title: Use tabs and splits
term-tabs.body: Click + to find another host, or split the focused shell to the right or down with the shortcuts below. Drag a host or tab to a pane edge to split there, then drag the divider to resize.

term-workspaces.title: Save a workspace
term-workspaces.body: Use the workspace button to save your open tabs and splits. Pick a saved workspace from the sidebar or choose Restore last session when the terminal is empty.

term-header.title: Move, zoom, and watch panes
term-header.body: In a split tab, drag a pane by its header, use its zoom button, or use its broadcast toggle while broadcast is on. Right-click the header to watch for output or 30 seconds of silence, and look for accent dots marking unread output.

term-layout.title: Arrange panes and sync scrolling
term-layout.body: Open the Layout menu to tile panes evenly, equalize existing splits, or sync scrolling. After tiling or equalizing, you have five seconds to select Undo.

term-broadcast.title: Type in several panes
term-broadcast.body: Toggle broadcast to send keystrokes to every included pane with an amber frame. Broadcasting pauses while a pane is zoomed.

term-footer.title: Read the footer chips
term-footer.body: Check the footer for broadcast status, watches, and synced scrolling. When a remote program requests mouse input, click the mouse chip to switch between selection and app mouse control.

term-smart.title: Use command suggestions and alerts
term-smart.body: With suggestions enabled, press → to accept the faded completion at the prompt. Enable long-command notifications in Terminal settings to get an alert when a long command finishes out of sight.

term-shortcuts.title: Keep shortcuts handy
term-shortcuts.body: Use the keys below to find hosts, copy and paste; the empty terminal lists the rest. Replay this tour from the empty terminal or from Settings › About in the main window.
